title: Chart and KPI Definitions
summary: Defines exact formulas, bucket logic, event taxonomy, and scoring heuristics used by dashboard visuals.
coverage: Data quality dependencies and staleness effects

sections.title: Calculation windows and limits
paragraphs: Dashboard calculations use fixed windows and display limits to preserve comparability over time. Current defaults are 30 days for recent activity windows and 6 months for trend buckets.
Recent activity, top-risk assets, and tester workload lists are also capped to maintain readable visual density.

sections.title: KPI formulas
paragraphs: KPI values are computed from live record and pentest datasets. The formulas below match current frontend calculation logic.

rows: count where status is `In Progress` or `Completed`
Returns `0` when no vulnerable assets exist.
count completed with `test_end_date` in last 30 days
sum of vulnerability counts for non-fixed records
Can exceed asset count when records contain multiple findings.

sections.title: Trend series definitions
paragraphs: Trend lines are monthly bucketed. Started and completed series track testing throughput. Detected and resolved series track vulnerability movement.
For vulnerability trend counts, RAPTOR uses parsed `vulnerabilities` arrays when available. If array data is absent and record is marked vulnerable, it contributes one indicator.

sections.title: Recent changes event definitions
paragraphs: Recent changes feed consolidates pentest lifecycle events and inventory scope updates. Event timestamps are rendered as relative age when recent, then compact date labels for older entries.
Event types are normalized into five categories so management review can quickly separate throughput progress from risk emergence and scope drift.

rows: status completed with `test_end_date` in last 30 days.
record has vulnerability indicator with qualifying recent date.
record status is `updated` with recent modification timestamp.
record status is `missing` with recent modification timestamp.

sections.title: Top-risk and workload scoring
paragraphs: Top-risk assets use a composite score to prioritize attention. Workload rows are sorted first by open-risk burden, then by in-progress volume, then by total assignments.
These heuristics are intentionally simple and explainable so managers can validate prioritization without opaque scoring models.

rows: `testedApps / totalApps` using records with assigned app identity.
Records lacking app assignment are tracked separately from app coverage denominator.
